lines.text: Outlook.com has started bouncing some email, and Microsoft did not announce it.
Email has three checks. SPF lists allowed senders. DKIM signs the message. DMARC ties them to the From address.
lines.title: Three email checks

lines.text: Domains with no DMARC record may now see some messages rejected, even from small senders.
lines.title: Outlook.com now

lines.text: The bounce says the message lacks authentication records, even when SPF already works.
lines.title: What happens

lines.text: Only some messages bounce, so a sender can easily think everything is fine.
The fix is one DNS record, named underscore dmarc, with the value v equals DMARC1, p equals none.
lines.title: The fix

lines.text: Check your domain with dig, and add the record. It blocks nothing else.
lines.title: Takeaways
